blocks.text: You can add WebSocket Controls to use as part of your AppProtection profiles in the Zscaler Admin Console. To learn more, see About WebSocket Controls.
To add a new WebSocket control:

blocks.item: Go to Private Access > Private App Protection > Protection Controls > WebSocket Controls.
Click Add.
The Add WebSocket Custom Control window appears.
In the Add WebSocket Custom Control window, complete the following steps:
Control Details
Control Name: Enter a name for the WebSocket control. The name cannot contain special characters, with the exception of periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).
Control Type: Select an option:
Request: Select if you want the WebSocket control to act as a message from the client to the server for the request. Select an option from the Request Control Type drop-down menu:
Max Payload Size: The maximum payload size control parameter.
Max Fragments Per Message: The maximum fragments for each message control parameter.
Response: Select if you want the WebSocket control to act as a response from the server to the client for the request. Select an option from the Response Control Type drop-down menu:
Max Payload Size: The maximum payload size control parameter.
Max Fragments Per Message: The maximum fragments for each message control parameter.
Description: (Optional) Enter a description.
Click Next.
See image.
Control Definition
Settings on the Control Definition tab depend on what you selected on the Control Details tab. These settings define how Private Access (ZPA) inspects user traffic.
To set the control:
For either Max Payload Size or Max Fragments Per Message, enter the value for that specific parameter. Use the arrow icons to adjust the value.
Control Action: Select how user traffic is handled for the control parameters selected on the Control Details tab:
Allow: The user is allowed to proceed with the control parameters you set.
Block: The user receives a 403 response code for the control parameters you set.
Click Next.
See image.
Severity
Severity: Select the severity level for the WebSocket custom control:
Critical: The greatest level of concern.
High: The second greatest level of concern.
Medium: The third greatest level of concern.
Low: The least level of concern.
In addition to severity levels, WebSocket custom controls have a paranoia level of 1 as they are used in an AppProtection profile.
Click Next.
See image.
Review
On the Review tab, review the custom control configurations.
See image.
Click Save.
